description.narrative:
The objective of this support is Building Inclusive and Multi-dimensional Approaches and Capacities for Effective Conflict Prevention in Africa.
The intervention covers 3 result areas: 1) Enhanced Institutional Responses of the AU and RECS to Prevent Complex Conflicts 2) Strengthened Capacities of National and Local Infrastructures for Effective Conflict Prevention 3) Enhanced Evidence Based Analysis to Inform Policy Support and Knowledge Production for Conflict Prevention
Key constituencies to the programme include local, national, and regional structures, such as the AU, RECs/RMs (IGAD, SADC, ECCAS), and other organisations such as the United Cities and Local Governments; Youth focused and youth-led organisations, Women focused, and women led organisations and Networks (FemWise-Africa and GIMAC); Community leaders; and Faith-based and traditional leaders.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

title.narrative: African Centre for the Constructive Resolution of Dispute (ACCORD)

description.narrative:
ACCORDs contribution has resulted in significant advances in conflict prevention, mediation capacity, and policy influence across local, national, and regional levels.
A total of 383 participants (77% women) were capacitated in conflict prevention and mediation skills, with 80% of surveyed stakeholders reporting an increased ability to prevent, manage, or resolve conflict. These efforts translated into tangible outcomes, with participants demonstrating diffusion effects by sharing knowledge within their communities, institutions, and professional networks.
At the continental level, ACCORD strengthened institutional mediation frameworks through continued collaboration with the African Union (AU). This included contributions to the revision of the AU Mediation Handbook and the development of gender-sensitive early warning frameworks. Members of FemWise-Africa gained enhanced skills to design mediation strategies and improved understanding of AU mediation processes. ACCORD also played a key role in the establishment and expansion of womens mediation networks, including the launch of the FemWise-South Sudan local chapter and the broader Women Mediators Network in Southern Africa, with national chapters such as in the DRC. These efforts strengthened mediation and conflict prevention capacities among women mediators in the DRC and ECCAS regions.
At the regional level, ACCORD engaged with the Southern African Development Community (SADC) to support the development and review of its Youth, Peace and Security (YPS) Strategy, contributing to its validation and anticipated adoption in 2025. ACCORD also provided input into broader AU and IGAD YPS policy processes, including the IGAD Youth Policy Implementation Roadmap.
Nationally, ACCORD contributed to advancing the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda in South Africa, including support for the establishment and ongoing implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) on UNSCR 1325. This included promoting awareness, knowledge, and capacity development related to the NAP among local stakeholders.
At the community level, ACCORD strengthened grassroots peace infrastructures and local actor capacities. Civil society organisations, including the Council of Swaziland Churches, gained skills to operationalise local peace committees, contributing to conflict prevention in politically sensitive environments. Engagement with faith-based actors helped reinforce their role in mediation and community-level peacebuilding. Similarly, REFWOMEN participants demonstrated increased mediation knowledge and initiated local peace activities, while Mozambican youth were trained in conflict prevention and encouraged to participate in national dialogue processes.
ACCORD also supported knowledge generation and dissemination, with its publications (such as the African Journal on Conflict Resolution and Conflict Trends) widely used by practitioners80100% of respondents reported these resources as useful to their work.
Overall, these results demonstrate ACCORDs multi-level approach to conflict prevention, combining capacity building, institutional strengthening, policy engagement, and knowledge production to create sustained and scalable impact across Africa.
